Thong Krut is a small fishing village on Samui's south-west coast, and its pier is where boats leave for Koh Madsum (Pig Island), Koh Tan and Koh Rap, about 15–30 minutes offshore depending on the boat. It is 13 km (20–25 minutes) from Lamai and 24 km (35–40 minutes) from Chaweng. Our Pig Island tours start at 1,450 THB per adult and run all year, including November and December when Ang Thong is closed. The village has a few seafood restaurants and good late-afternoon views, but its tidal shore is not a swimming beach.

Map of Thong Krut

Thong Krut sits at the western end of Samui's south coast, between Laem Sor in the east and Taling Ngam in the north-west. Koh Tan (Koh Taen) is the large island directly offshore, with Koh Madsum just to its east and Koh Rap further out.

The pier: what leaves from Thong Krut

Thong Krut is the gateway to the small islands south-west of Samui. Speedboats and wooden longtails load at the pier and along the shore, and the crossing is short and usually calmer than the east coast because the south-west is sheltered from the north-east monsoon.

Getting to Thong Krut

There are two ways in by road, and both end on quiet village lanes.

From Lamai, Chaweng and the east

Follow the ring road (Route 4169) south-west past Hua Thanon and the Na Muang junction, then turn south towards the coast and follow signs for Thong Krut, Laem Sor or Bang Kao. From Lamai this is about 13 km and 20–25 minutes, the shortest run from any main beach area.

From Nathon, Lipa Noi and the west

Route 4170 links Lipa Noi and Taling Ngam with the south coast. It is the scenic option, but it is steep and narrow with blind bends, and slippery when wet; in October–December low-lying stretches in the south-west can flood after heavy rain. Ride slowly, and avoid it on a scooter if you are not experienced.

Road distances; times for normal daytime traffic. Fares are typical 2026 ranges and taxis have no meters. Grab will take you to Thong Krut, but drivers are scarce here for the return, so arrange your ride back in advance or use our hotel transfer. Songthaews rarely run this far south-west.

Parking: there is free parking by the pier for cars and scooters. Leave nothing valuable on a scooter, lock helmets to the bike, and don't park on boat ramps or in front of village houses. More on getting around Koh Samui and Samui's roads.

Pier day: practical tips

  • Arrive 30 minutes early if you are meeting a boat yourself; most boats load in the morning.
  • Cash: bring at least 50 THB per person for the Koh Madsum fee plus small notes for drinks; don't count on finding an ATM at the pier.
  • Tide: at low tide boats may load from the end of the pier or from the shallows, and you may wade a short way. Water shoes help. Check the tide below.
  • Sun: longtails have limited shade. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat and water.
  • Dry bag: phones and cameras get splashed on any small boat.
  • The pigs: don't chase them, pick up piglets or feed them junk food; give them shade and space in the heat.

Hiring a longtail yourself

You can charter a longtail directly at Thong Krut. Boatmen usually offer Koh Madsum and Koh Tan, and prices are mostly fixed, though polite bargaining is acceptable. In 2026 a private half-day longtail (about 4 hours) to Pig Island and Koh Tan costs roughly 3,500–6,000 THB per boat on the open market, without transfers. Check that every passenger gets a life jacket that fits, agree in advance which islands you will visit and for how long, and confirm whether the Madsum fee is included. Don't go out with any boat when the sea is rough. If you prefer it organised, with transfers, life jackets for children and snorkel gear, see our private longtail.

The village and seafood

Thong Krut is a working fishing village with a handful of large seafood restaurants facing the sea and simple shops. Expect fresh fish, prawns, squid and crab sold by weight, plus standard Thai dishes; ask the price per kilo before you order. It is a good place for lunch after a morning boat trip. For a bigger choice, the island's best southern seafood restaurant, Baan Suan Lung Khai (MICHELIN Bib Gourmand 2026, reservation required), is a few kilometres north-west in Taling Ngam. There is no nightlife in Thong Krut. See Koh Samui seafood and our Taling Ngam guide.

The beach and swimming

Thong Krut sits on a shallow, sandy bay. At high tide the beach is pleasant for a stroll with views of the islands; at low tide it turns into wide flats, and around the pier the water is full of moored boats. It is not a swimming beach. Swim on the islands instead: Koh Madsum's beach and Koh Tan's reef are 15–30 minutes away. The south-west coast is sheltered from the October–December north-east monsoon, so conditions here are often calmer than at Chaweng or Lamai, though November is still the wettest month island-wide (about 445 mm) and boats can be cancelled on bad days.

Sunset at Thong Krut

The coast here faces south and south-west, with Koh Tan and Koh Madsum on the horizon, so late afternoons have long golden light over the water. For the sun dropping straight into the sea behind the Five Islands, drive 10–15 minutes north-west to Taling Ngam, or see it from the water on our Pig Island sunset tour. Sunset times range from about 17:55 in November to 18:45 in July. More spots on Koh Samui sunset spots.

Where to stay near Thong Krut

Thong Krut has a few small resorts and holiday villas near the village, and the clifftop and beachfront resorts of Taling Ngam are 10–15 minutes away. This corner suits people who want quiet, sunsets and an early start for the islands, and who are happy to drive 35–50 minutes to Chaweng, the airport or the Koh Phangan piers. Restaurant choice is small and evenings are very quiet. See where to stay on Koh Samui and villas.

Nearby sights

  • Chinese Temple of Guanyin (9.4212, 99.9479): a Chinese temple just west of the village, open in daylight.
  • Laem Sor Pagoda: the gold-tiled seafront chedi 2.5 km east, 07:00–18:00, free.
  • Bang Kao and the south coast: quiet beaches and wellness resorts.
  • Taling Ngam: the Five Islands sunset and the Bib Gourmand seafood restaurant.
  • Na Muang waterfalls: 20 minutes inland, 09:00–17:00.

What's not open near Thong Krut

Older maps show a Samui Snake Farm on the Thong Krut and Taling Ngam side. We could find no current hours or prices for it in 2026, so we don't list it as open; we'll update this if it is confirmed. The separate Samui Aquarium and Tiger Zoo on the Laem Set side also has an unclear status, and we don't recommend animal shows.
